triples.relationship: same-book motif of divinely sent winds
triples.rationale: God commands a scorching wind on land, and the text then reports the sun striking Jonah's head. Earlier the Lord stirred up a wind at sea, explicitly followed by a great surge. Both episodes feature divinely directed winds, while describing their accompanying events differently.
triples.source_text: As the sun rose, God commanded a burning, scorching wind. The sun struck Jonah’s head; he lost heart, renounced his life and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.”

target_units.text: The Lord stirred up a wind upon the sea, and there was a great surge on the sea; the ship was in danger of being shattered.
